newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican feeder head weekly exports, imports - USDA.
newsitem.headline: Mexican feeder head weekly exports, imports - USDA.

text.p: USDA said Monday that steer calves and yearlings exported from Mexico to the United States sold one to two cents higher than the previous week.
Exports for the week were estimated at 6,000 head into Texas and New Mexico. Confirmed exports for the prior week totaled 6,999 head against 6,703 head in the same 1996 week.
"Trade active, demand good. Bulk of supply consisted of medium and large steers weighing 300-600 lb. Also, several lots of corriente steers crossed," USDA said.

Prices for feeder steers weighing 300-400 lbs were 79-89 cents a lb, although a few lots sold at 90 cents for 300-lb head. For 400-500 lbs prices were 70-79 cents and for 500-600 lbs they were 68-70 cents/lb
Imports of slaughter cows were estimated to have totaled 4,000 head for the week with good demand, USDA added.
